notes: τῷ πρώτῳ is the main judgment call: rule 102 is unanimous that a Greek article governing a substantival adjective takes both the determiner and the supplied nominal, so belonging to the … man is the article's and chief stands bare. Rule 17's generic-noun clause was rejected because it is scoped to anarthrous Greek.

The supplied frame belonging to rides with the article that carries the English determiner (rules 21, 67), and rule 67's bar on heading a frame's supplied noun is not in question — man is the article's own nominal, not the frame's.
τοῖς περὶ … → the neighborhood is a substantival article whose modifier is a prepositional phrase; περί keeps its own of under rule 36.
